claims.text: When firm.yaml's paths.thresholds names a file that is not there, the workspace refuses the case naming that file ('no such file'), as `cma run --thresholds` does, instead of raising indicators from the packaged thresholds (R14; design failure modes 'no case opens with different flags'). FirmConfig now records which paths firm.yaml named (named / names_path); case_thresholds() loads the named file whether or not it exists, and falls back to the packaged thresholds only when firm.yaml names none and the default indicators.yaml is absent.
claims.proof_cmd: python -m pytest -v tests/test_workspace_indicators.py -k "names_but_missing or no_firm_thresholds or distinct_ids"

claims.text: The indicators panel now shows which thresholds file the indicators were raised from (thresholds.source), marked when it is the one shipped with the tool; and indicator section element ids carry the account (indicator-<account>-<id>), so two accounts' I1 no longer collide.
Lint, compile, the full suite and the marker tiers pass.

dispositions.finding: major: case_thresholds() falls back to the packaged thresholds whenever the configured path does not exist, including when firm.yaml explicitly names a firm thresholds file (src/cma/review/summary.py:128); the page does not show thresholds.source.
dispositions.evidence: The new test test_a_thresholds_file_firm_yaml_names_but_missing_shows_no_figures failed before the change (state 'shown' with shipped thresholds). firm.load() now records the paths firm.yaml names (FirmConfig.named, names_path), and case_thresholds() calls ind.load_thresholds on a named path, which raises ThresholdsError 'no such file', shown as a refusal with no figures or queue. The panel now prints 'Thresholds from <source>' (test_with_no_firm_thresholds_file_the_shipped_ones_raise_the_indicators, which failed before).

dispositions.finding: minor: indicator ids restart at I1 per account, so a two-account page has duplicate id="indicator-I1" elements.
dispositions.evidence: Section ids are now indicator-<account>-<id> (summary.py _indicators_html); test_indicator_sections_of_two_accounts_have_distinct_ids asserts indicator-main-I1 and indicator-second-I1 and no duplicates. The queue entry still names the indicator alongside its account column.

dispositions.finding: minor: the performance claim (0.529 s for 10,000 lines) cites scratchpad/perf.py, which no runner tier ran; unpaged rendering of a large queue is unproven.
dispositions.evidence: Not a code defect: the claim was unproven, so this claim.json makes no performance claim. Paging and R52's timing belong to T22's timed recompute, not to this task.

notes: Only a path firm.yaml names explicitly is required to exist; the default indicators.yaml at the case root is still optional, keeping the packaged thresholds as the default. FirmConfig gains an additive defaulted field (named), so existing constructions are unchanged.
